brief: Lane mr3: make Metal hybrid batching of the 35B faster. Give GatedDeltaNet conv / delta rule, the QK-norm-rope-KV prologue and the split-KV attention a row axis (one dispatch over all rows, state and KV through a device-address row table, as CUDA R3), bitwise equal to the solo step; decode fp8/nvfp4 weights once for all rows in the multi-row GEMVs; measure cap 16; no-op with batching off. Hard stop 2026-10-24 10:30 EDT.
hypothesis: The step grows about 3.8 ms per extra row because GDN and attention launch once per row (240 + 240 + 80 + 80 launches per step at B = 8). One launch per op over a row axis removes most of that, bitwise by construction.

verdict: Row-table kernels for GDN conv / delta rule, the QK-norm-rope-KV prologue and the split-KV attention make the Metal 35B batched step 6 / 11 / 15% faster at B = 2 / 4 / 8 (in process) and 512-generated aggregate +11% / +23% at 4 / 8 streams (154.4 / 161.6 to 171.5 / 199.1); 128-generated +6% / +8%; single stream unchanged. Bitwise to the solo step. Cap stays 8 (16 measured +3%).
summary: Row-table kernels for GDN conv / delta rule, the QK-norm-rope-KV prologue and the split-KV attention make the Metal 35B batched step 6 / 11 / 15% faster at B = 2 / 4 / 8 (in process) and 512-generated aggregate +11% / +23% at 4 / 8 streams (154.4 / 161.6 to 171.5 / 199.1); 128-generated +6% / +8%; single stream unchanged. Bitwise to the solo step. Cap stays 8 (16 measured +3%).
lessons: The per-row launches were 14% of the B = 8 step in-process; after removing them the remaining ~2.9 ms per row is the multi-row fp8 / nvfp4 GEMV arithmetic, not launch overhead.
Decoding the e4m3 / e2m1 weight chunk once for all rows of a multi-row GEMV is bitwise (same fma chain per row) and saves ~2.8 ms of the B = 8 step.

A negative control for a position-dependent kernel needs data that makes the accumulation order visible: random data gave 0 differing bytes between the host-position and device-position attention, +-2^20 cancelling values gave 44k of 82k.
Chunking a 9..16-row call into two 8-row launches is row-exact but re-reads the weights: 12 rows are slower than 8, 16 rows only +3%.
